name: Guinea
tagline: The water tower of West Africa
summary: The Niger, the Senegal and the Gambia all rise in the Fouta Djallon, a sandstone highland of waterfalls and cliffs — and Conakry has produced more of the region's music than anywhere except Bamako.
when: November to March. The Fouta is best just after the rains, when the falls are still running.

entries.caption: The Fouta Djallon
entries.description: A sandstone highland at a thousand metres, cut by gorges, and the source of three great rivers.
entries.subject: green plateau and sandstone cliffs in the Fouta Djallon

entries.caption: Where the Rivers Rise
entries.description: The Niger, the Senegal and the Gambia all begin within a hundred kilometres of each other.
entries.subject: a clear stream running over rock at the source of the Niger

entries.caption: Chimpanzees at Bossou
entries.description: One of the best-studied wild chimpanzee groups anywhere, and one that uses stone tools.
entries.subject: a wild chimpanzee cracking nuts with a stone at Bossou

entries.caption: The Forest, Not the Plain
entries.description: There is no savanna circuit. What Guinea has is forest primates and the Nimba massif.
entries.subject: dense forest canopy on the slopes of Mount Nimba

entries.caption: Mount Nimba
entries.description: 1,752 metres on the Liberian border, with species that live on that mountain and nowhere else.
entries.subject: the grassy ridge of Mount Nimba above forest

entries.caption: Ditinn and Kinkon
entries.description: Ditinn drops a hundred metres off a sheer cliff; Kinkon runs through a gorge below Pita.
entries.subject: the Ditinn waterfall falling from a sheer cliff in the Fouta

entries.caption: The Upper Niger
entries.description: It rises near the Sierra Leone border and is already wide by the time it leaves the country.
entries.subject: the upper Niger river running broad through green country

entries.caption: Three Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Mangrove coast with the Iles de Los off Conakry, and beaches on Roume and Kassa.
entries.subject: a beach and palms on Roume island off Conakry

entries.caption: The Guinean Forest
entries.description: Ziama and Diecke in the southeast — some of the last high forest in West Africa.
entries.subject: buttressed rainforest trees in the Ziama massif

entries.caption: Hiking the Fouta
entries.description: Village to village between waterfalls and cliffs, with the best walking network in the region.
entries.subject: walkers on a path between villages in the Fouta Djallon

entries.caption: Where the Music Came From
entries.description: Bembeya Jazz, the Ballets Africains, and a state that funded orchestras for two decades.
entries.subject: a djembe and balafon group performing in Conakry

entries.caption: Fulani, Malinke, Susu
entries.description: Fulani in the Fouta, Malinke in the upper Niger country, Susu on the coast.
entries.subject: a Fulani herder with cattle on the Fouta Djallon plateau

entries.caption: Riz Gras and Fouti
entries.description: Rice with palm oil and fish, and the sour milk and maize of the Fouta.
entries.subject: a shared plate of Guinean rice with fish and sauce

entries.caption: Masked Dance in the Forest Region
entries.description: The forest peoples of the southeast keep mask societies that are not for visitors, and some that are.
entries.subject: a stilt dancer performing at a village festival in Guinea

entries.caption: Weaving and Indigo
entries.description: Fouta indigo cloth, Malinke weaving, and the leatherwork of the highland towns.
entries.subject: indigo-dyed cloth drying at a Fouta Djallon workshop

entries.caption: The Almamy's Fouta
entries.description: The Fouta Djallon was a theocratic Fulani state for a century and a half before the French came.
entries.subject: an old mosque and stone walls in a Fouta Djallon town

entries.caption: Nimba, Listed
entries.description: Mount Nimba is a World Heritage site for its endemic toad, viviparous, that lives on the ridge.
entries.subject: montane grassland and cloud on the Nimba ridge

entries.caption: Conakry
entries.description: A capital on a peninsula, with the Grande Mosquee and the sea on both sides.
entries.subject: the Grande Mosquee and low buildings of Conakry

entries.caption: Colonial and Fouta Vernacular
entries.description: French colonial in Conakry, and round thatched houses with painted walls in the highlands.
entries.subject: a round thatched Fouta house with a painted wall

entries.caption: Market Day in Labe
entries.description: The highland market fills with Fulani from every village within a day's walk.
entries.subject: the crowded weekly market at Labe in the Fouta Djallon

entries.caption: Waterfalls You Can Swim In
entries.description: Most of the Fouta's falls have a pool at the bottom and a path down to it.
entries.subject: children swimming in a pool below a Fouta Djallon waterfall

entries.caption: Trekking the Highlands
entries.description: The Fouta has marked routes, village guides and huts, which is rare in the region.
entries.subject: a marked walking trail across the Fouta Djallon plateau

entries.caption: Modest
entries.description: Hotels in Conakry and a few in Labe and Dalaba. The Fouta runs on homestays.
entries.subject: a colonial-era hill station guesthouse at Dalaba

entries.caption: Nimba's Endemics
entries.description: The mountain has species found on it and nowhere else, and an iron deposit under them.
entries.subject: a botanist recording plants on the Nimba grassland

entries.caption: Cliffs and Water
entries.description: The Fouta escarpments in the hour after the rain stops, when everything is running.
entries.subject: cliffs and multiple waterfalls after rain in the Fouta Djallon

entries.caption: The Dame de Mali
entries.description: A rock face near Mali-ville shaped like a woman's profile, at the top of the Fouta.
entries.subject: the Dame de Mali rock profile above the Fouta escarpment

entries.caption: Why Guinea
entries.description: The best walking in West Africa, and the rivers that made the whole region.
entries.subject: a walker looking out over layered Fouta Djallon ridges
